findings.title: Cache deletion does not invalidate connectedCalendars query
findings.body: `deleteCacheMutation` only calls `onSuccess?.()` and shows a toast on success. Unlike the disconnect mutation below it, it never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. The parent query in `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` uses `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`, and `onChanged` is optional, so after a successful cache deletion the dropdown can continue showing the old `cacheUpdatedAt` timestamp and "Delete cached data" action until some unrelated refetch happens. Add `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in the mutation's success/settled path.

findings.title: Cache status query includes expired CalendarCache rows
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all `CalendarCache` rows for a credential without filtering `expiresAt >= now`, while `getCachedAvailability` only treats non-expired rows as valid cache. If expired rows remain in the table, the UI will still show a cache status and timestamp for a credential whose cache is no longer usable. The query should filter to active rows, e.g. `where: { credentialId: { in: credentialIds }, expiresAt: { gte: new Date() } }`, unless showing historical rows is intentional.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is always formatted in en-US
findings.body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` is hardcoded even though the component obtains the user's locale via `useLocale()`. Users on non-English locales will see the cache timestamp formatted with US date/time conventions instead of their locale. Use the current locale or a shared date formatting utility.

findings.title: No test covers the cache deletion ownership check
findings.body: The new `deleteCache` endpoint enforces access by requiring the credential to belong to `user.id`, then deletes all `CalendarCache` rows for that credential. There are no added tests covering the key negative case: a user trying to delete cache for another user's credential should get an error and no rows should be deleted. This is the main security boundary of the new endpoint and should be covered by a unit or integration test.

findings.title: Existing cache rows get migration time as their last-updated timestamp
findings.body: The migration adds `updatedAt` with `DEFAULT NOW()`, so all pre-existing `CalendarCache` rows are backfilled with the migration/deploy time rather than the time the cache was actually written. Since `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` surfaces `max(updatedAt)` as the UI's "Last updated" value, users with existing cache entries will initially see a misleadingly recent timestamp. Consider backfilling from another source such as `expiresAt` minus the caching period, or otherwise noting the limitation.
